written.myAnswer: Different solutes have different solubilities in water because their particles differ in nature and interact differently with water. The section explains that sugar molecules are larger than salt ions, allowing more water molecules to surround a sugar molecule, so more sugar dissolves.

Solubility is the amount of solute that dissolves in a particular amount of solvent to form a saturated solution at a specified temperature. For most solid solutes, solubility increases as temperature rises, though the change depends on the solute.
